title: Start 'Em, Sit 'Em tight ends for Week 2 fantasy football
description: With tight end Brock Bowers dealing with injury and Colston Loveland posting a goose egg last week, who at the position can you trust in Week 2?
fullText:
Week 1 of the NFL season delivered plenty of surprises, but fantasy football managers must turn the page to Week 2.

It's tempting to overreact to one poor performance, but there's no reason to panic after just one game. Colston Loveland, for example, was held without a catch despite the Bears putting up 59 points. That's certainly frustrating, but it's far too early to hit the panic button.

Whether you're 1-0 or 0-1, a long fantasy football season still lies ahead.

Unfortunately, the injury bug has already hit the tight end position, with Brock Bowers undergoing a knee procedure and being listed as day-to-day heading into Week 2.

Fortunately, the position has plenty of depth, with promising young players joining a group of reliable veterans. For fantasy managers dealing with injuries or disappointing starts, the waiver wire could provide some intriguing streaming options this week.

Here is a breakdown of who you should start and who you should sit at tight end in Week 2:

The Buffalo Bills have their home opener this week on "Thursday Night Football" when they host the Detroit Lions. It's not your ordinary opener as they will unveil their new stadium.

Kincaid is a breakout candidate in 2026 and he ran 22 routes on 32 dropbacks by Josh Allen in Week 1. That's 69% route participation which is a jump from the 44.2% he averaged last season. He played 42-of-57 snaps overall, his highest mark since Week 9 of 2024. All point to fantasy goodness moving forward. He paced the position in receiving yards after one week with 130 against a tough Texans defense.

Detroit just allowed Saints tight ends Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant to combine for seven catches for 79 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1. With another big performance Kincaid would enter weekly must-start status.

The 31-year-old is back in weekly start territory when the Ravens host the New Orleans Saints in their home opener. Baltimore's passing game could funnel more opportunities his way with Zay Flowers dealing with a hamstring injury after exploding for 150 yards and a touchdown before leaving Week 1, while rookie Ja'Kobi Lane suffered a fractured wrist. That leaves Lamar Jackson with fewer established weapons, and Andrews remains one of his most trusted targets. Andrews had a 17.6% target share in the first half with Flowers on the field but that jumped to 42.9% in the second half after Flowers exited.

He also led Ravens tight ends with 49 snaps and caught four passes on six targets (which tied a team-high) in Week 1. Detroit's Sam LaPorta caught six passes for 57 yards against New Orleans in Week 1. Jackson looked comfortable operating Declan Doyle's offense, making Andrews an intriguing Week 2 play and bounce-back candidate this season.

The Chicago Bears battle the Minnesota Vikings in their 2026 home oepner in Week 2 and don't expect Loveland to be a non-factor like he was in Week 1. The former first-rounder had zero catches on two targets in the Bears Week 1 blowout over the Carolina Panthers.

Chicago's offense passed the eye test in Week 1, and head coach Ben Johnson has said he wants to make history. Caleb Williams can continue to target his wide receivers Rome Odunze, Luther Burden and Kalif Raymond along with veteran tight end Cole Kmet but the upside is too immense for the 22 year-old.

Chicago traded DJ Moore to the Buffalo Bills and Loveland finished his rookie campaign strong with 25 targets across Chicago's two playoff games. In his last 12 games combined, he caught 59 passes for 790 yards and six TDs. Those stats reaffirm why we're not panicking, and neither should you. He ran 34 of a possible 38 routes in Week 1 so expect those to formulate into fantasy points moving forward.

The veteran in New England is stepping back into a familiar role after A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain. Brown was placed on injured reserve, meaning he'll miss at least four games. Henry had a 17% target share and 74% route share last season. The Patriots offense struggled to put long drives together in Week 1, but should have better success against the Pittsburgh Steelers defense at home.

There's little target competition outside of 32-year-old Mack Hollins and free agent aquisition Romeo Doubs who struggled in the opener. Henry lit up Pittsburgh last season to the tune of eight receptions on 11 targets for 90 receiving yards and two touchdowns. In fact, he's had multiple touchdowns in 3 of 4 career matchups against the Steelers. Expect Drake Maye to bounce back and lean on his security blanket.

Trevor Lawrence and Strange connected on two of three targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in Week 1. Jacksonville's next matchup comes on the road at Mile High against the Denver Broncos.

Denver allowed Travis Kelce to break loose for a 59-yard catch in Week 1, but take that mistake away and the future Hall of Famer would have finished with a measly two-catch, 12-yard day. Lawrence has plenty of mouths to feed with a trio of wide receivers in Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, and Brian Thomas Jr., which pushes Strange further down the pecking order. The Broncos defense will likely come into their home opener looking to right the ship after a poor Week 1 performance.

One of the most popular waiver wire recommendations for Week 2 is a recommended sit. Unfortunately for managers who roster someone like Bowers and hoped to find gold in Gesicki this week, it's a poor matchup.

The Cincinnati Bengals hit the road to face the Houston Texans, who were the NFL's No. 1 defense in 2025. In Week 1, Kincaid made his mark against Houston, but don't expect that trend to continue. With Azeez Al-Shaair patrolling the middle of the field, it's difficult for most tight ends to have big days against this Texans defense.

Week 1 was an outlier for Gesicki, who failed to reach double-digit fantasy points in all but two games last season. After Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins' slow start last week, Joe Burrow will likely get them more involved in Week 2. You don't have to leave Gesicki on waivers, but you should make arrangements to keep him out of lineups this week.

title: Phillies can't live in fear of another playoff bullpen debacle
description: Phillies' World Series hopes hinge on this group after three straight October disasters.
fullText:
WASHINGTON — There are 12 former All-Stars and at least two future Hall of Famers occupying the Philadelphia Phillies clubhouse on a given day. This collection of well-paid, salty, accomplished stars will command most of the attention as the Phillies attempt, for the fifth consecutive year, to bring a World Series title home to Philly.

Then there is Jonathan Bowlan, an easygoing dude from Memphis, quiet and forthright, making his way through his first full season in the big leagues. Bowlan might not realize it yet, but he may have more to do with whether the Phillies raise a trophy in October than any of the superstars.

Bowlan, 26, has emerged as the Phillies' primary set-up man, aiming, along with 25-year-old Orion Kerkering, to form a bridge between the club's quartet of ace starting pitchers and their dominant closer, Jhoan Duran.

It is thankless work, and the sixth through 10th innings are exactly where the Phillies' prior championship quests have gone awry. Lately, they've been trouble spots as the club staggers down the stretch to finalize a National League wild-card berth.

Bowlan has given up a run in five consecutive appearances entering Wednesday, Sept. 16, including late-game homers in three of those; Kerkering gave up runs in four of his last five games, including multiple-run outings in Phillies losses.

"Those innings," says interim manager Don Mattingly, "are always the stressful innings.

"And you'd like to be able to lock down that end of the game when you get a lead or you're in a close game."

Mattingly was speaking after Bowlan gave up a first-pitch, three-run, pinch-hit homer to Daylen Lile in the seventh inning of a 6-3 loss to Washington, the latest setback that imperiled the club's wild-card standing. Oh, the team's still on fairly firm ground, with a 95% chance to reach the playoffs, according to FanGraphs.

It's just that the Phillies keep slipping down the pecking order and, with a rough combo of a flailing lineup and slumping bullpen, inspiring little confidence in their postseason chances.

For Bowlan, learning to cope has come before having to face the bright lights of the postseason. He's found that in reflecting on failure, there's a fine line between quickly moving on and interrogating what went wrong.

"There's definitely times I lose some sleep at night, for sure," Bowlan tells USA TODAY Sports. "But as soon as you wake up the next morning, it's a new day. It's a blessing. God woke me up to continue on. And you can't live in the past. Because you can learn from your experiences, for sure. And that's what I continue to try and do.

"It's taken some time to learn that, about the short memory. But I've gotten to the point where, 'Yeah, you can think about it a little bit.' And there's times where it was a tough thing to happen in that situation.

"But you live and you learn. All you can do is just keep chugging along. Keep moving."

That ethos certainly applies to the Phillies, who won't glean any sympathy from rival fanbases, given their four-year run of success powered by an aggressive ownership group bent on winning their first World Series since 2008.

Yet every bite at the apple ends rottenly for all but one team every year. And October's late innings have been a long-running soap opera in Philly.

In 2022, it was Jose Alvarado, relieving ace Zack Wheeler in the sixth inning of World Series Game 6, the Phillies leading 1-0, only to give up a left-on-left three-run blast to Yordan Alvarez, enabling the Houston Astros to nail down the championship.

A year later, it was the rookie Kerkering – with just eight major league appearances under his belt – summoned to protect a 1-0 lead in the seventh inning of NLCS Game 3, the Phillies nine outs from seizing a 3-0 lead on the ostensibly overmatched Arizona Diamondbacks.

Instead, Kerkering gave up three consecutive hits, including Lourdes Gurriel's RBI double, to tie the game and set the stage for closer Craig Kimbrel yielding a walk-off hit, one of Kimbrel's many failings in that series. The Diamondbacks won in seven games.

In 2024, the goats were numerous – from Alvarado to Carlos Estevez to Jeff Hoffman, who yielded six earned runs and recorded four outs across three games – as the Mets pulled off a stunning NLDS upset.

And last year, it was Kerkering, aiming to keep the Phillies alive in the 11th inning of NLDS Game 4 at Los Angeles, but infamously fielding Andy Pages' two-out ground ball and throwing home instead of taking an easy out at first.

Now, Kerkering realizes that staying true to himself is just as important in the aftermath as breaking down pitches that backfired or physical errors. And even his recent struggles have provided teachable moments.

"You look at some of those struggles you've gone through the last couple years and just try to learn a lot more," says Kerkering, "since I came up through the system so fast and wasn't able to really go through those downs. I think going through them now a little bit has been super-helpful. You'll go on some great runs and some not-so-fun runs. But that's what baseball is. It's a game of failure.

"You just try to make sure you get back on who you're supposed to be as a person."

Bowlan's recent struggles have overshadowed his excellent work most of this season. He's blown five saves but also has a 1.04 WHIP and struck out 71 in 55 innings.

It's been a startling rise for Bowlan, who admitted he was a bit stunned – "Kind of a whoa moment," he says – when the Phillies acquired him over the winter for longtime lefty reliever Matt Strahm. The Phillies' suggestion he lean more heavily on his four-seam fastball – its usage has risen from 33.6% to 48% - has paid significant dividends.

That will be his best friend come the postseason, waters he's looking forward to navigating.

"I've heard that being in the playoffs is one of the best experiences you can have in this game," says Bowlan. "Being in that situation, from what I've learned, you've got to just slow things down. You can't let things overwhelm you. These guys have been through it. They've been through big situations.

"I'm just trying to learn from them to the best of my ability."

Both Bowlan and Kerkering are operating a rung higher than the Phillies anticipated this season. They signed right-hander Brad Keller to a two-year, $22 million deal over the winter after his stellar 2025 with the Chicago Cubs. But Keller struggled into June, missed a month with forearm tendinitis and then tore the UCL in his throwing elbow in July.

Veteran lefties Alvarado, Brooks Raley and Tim Mayza balance out the bullpen, but aren't necessarily built for one-inning, high-leverage situations.

That's just one reason why Bowlan and Kerkering will be front and center this postseason.

Kerkering is now in his third full major league season, yet maintains he's "still the pup" on a club with 10-year vets like Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber, Trea Turner and Zack Wheeler. He has been through the postseason fire, for better or worse, and knows what he'll tell Bowlan before his October indoctrination.

"Think of it like you're playing the Dodgers, you're playing the Braves' series – (multiply) that by five," says Kerkering. "The intensity, how much people care, how much louder and the passion.

"But you still have to make your pitches. It's a big moment for the pitcher, a big moment for the hitters. It doesn't matter how long they've been there. You're battling each other out and there's very few teams left.

"You're highlighted, basically."

And the spotlight is about to get a lot brighter.

title: 'It will be a tricky game' - Maresca on Norwich test
description: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says he expects a "tricky game" against Championship side Norwich City in the Carabao Cup on Thursday evening, and has hinted at rotating his starting XI.  Maresca confirmed he will hand goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli his first competitive appearance for the club since signing from Marseille in the summer.
fullText:
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says he expects a "tricky game" against Championship side Norwich City in the Carabao Cup on Thursday evening, and has hinted at rotating his starting XI.

"We prepare all the games trying to win and trying to compete to win the competition," he said. "Then, at the end, we see if we are able to win or not.

"For sure, the game will be a tricky game because the one-off games are the difficult ones. We are going to try to win the game and then we will see."

Maresca confirmed he will hand goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli his first competitive appearance for the club since signing from Marseille in the summer.

"I was doing the same also in Chelsea and Leicester. We are going to give Rulli minutes."

He also hinted that Erling Haaland may be one of his first-team players given a rest after a gruelling week which involved wins in the Champions League at Porto and at Manchester United in the Premier League.

"Erling is one of the players that played 90 minutes back-to-back against Porto and Manchester United. He is not the only one," added Maresca.

"I think we have six or seven players who have played 90, 90. Some of them, not all of them, will probably need some rest."

title: New York Knicks sign NBA champion who played all 82 games for Nuggets last season
description: The New York Knicks have made another offseason move after winning the title earlier this year. While Mitchell Robinson departed for the Boston Celtics, the Knicks have signed several new players.
fullText:
The New York Knicks have made another offseason move after winning the title earlier this year. While Mitchell Robinson departed for the Boston Celtics, the Knicks have signed several new players.

Veteran center Andre Drummond is the only player to have joined the Knicks on a guaranteed deal this summer. However, Ochoa Agbaji, John Konchar, James Wiseman and Drew Eubanks have all signed non-guaranteed deals ahead of training camp.

The Knicks have also added an NBA champion to the roster who played all 82 regular-season games for the Denver Nuggets last year. He appears to be the most likely of all the training camp additions to make their full roster.

Shams Charania reported on Wednesday that the New York Knicks had signed Bruce Brown to a training camp contract. Brown became a free agent after leaving the Denver Nuggets and failing to find a guaranteed deal elsewhere.

Brown's reputation is not quite what it was when he helped the Nuggets win the championship in 2023. He averaged 12 points and four rebounds per game during that postseason run, earning a lucrative contract with the Indiana Pacers.

However, after difficult spells with the Pacers, Toronto Raptors and New Orleans Pelicans, Brown returned to Denver last season. He averaged 7.9 points per game and played in all 82 regular-season games, proving he can still be an effective role player.

Brown can play either shooting guard or small forward, although neither position is an obvious area of need for the Knicks' roster. They already have Landry Shamet, Jordan Clarkson and Miles McBride in the rotation, but Brown would offer something different as a more defensively minded guard.

title: Premier League Gameweek 4 Review: Biggest Talking Points and Takeaways
description: The English Premier League Gameweek 4 gave us plenty to talk about, with Arsenal maintaining their perfect start to the season and staying at the top of the table. Some of the other big teams, however, dropped points during another busy weekend of action. Manchester City claimed bragging rights in the Manchester derby with a […]
fullText:
The English Premier League Gameweek 4 gave us plenty to talk about, with Arsenal maintaining their perfect start to the season and staying at the top of the table. Some of the other big teams, however, dropped points during another busy weekend of action.

Manchester City claimed bragging rights in the Manchester derby with a narrow win over Manchester United, while Brighton & Hove Albion and Leeds United picked up impressive victories.

Chelsea were also held by Hull City, adding another surprise result to the weekend.

With four rounds now completed, some teams are starting to make a strong impression while others have raised more questions. There were also standout performances, unexpected results and a few issues that could shape what comes next.

Here are the biggest talking points and takeaways from Gameweek 4:

Arsenal remain one of the most reliable teams for Fantasy Premier League managers after another strong result. Their 2-0 win over Sunderland made it four wins from four, while they also kept another clean sheet.

David Raya was one of the standout performers after saving a penalty, while Bukayo Saka scored from the spot. Arsenal's defence has also continued to look strong, making their defenders and goalkeeper attractive options for managers looking for reliable points.

The same can be said about their attacking players, Arsenal have shown that they can deliver at both ends of the pitch, which makes their key players difficult to overlook as we move into the next few Gameweeks.

Chelsea were unable to beat newly promoted Hull City, but the 2-2 draw should not completely change how FPL managers view their attacking players.

The Blues have shown plenty of potential going forward, and Joao Pedro continued that trend by scoring and providing an assist against Hull City. Their attacking options remain attractive, even though their defensive performances have caused some concern.

For FPL managers, the main question is whether Chelsea can turn their attacking threat into more consistent results. Their next few fixtures should give us a better idea of which players are worth keeping in our plans.

Fabian Hurzeler's men produced one of the biggest results of the weekend by beating Coventry City 5-0. It was a dominant display and naturally put several of their players on the radar.

Pascal Grob was the standout performer, scoring once and providing two assists. Other Brighton players also picked up useful FPL returns, giving managers more options to consider.

However, it is important not to make a transfer simply because a player had one big Gameweek. Brighton's upcoming fixtures, along with each player's role and minutes, should also be considered before making a move.

Morgan Gibbs-White is another player who is starting to attract more attention after Nottingham Forest's 2-1 win over Aston Villa.

The midfielder provided an assist and continued his strong start to the season. His involvement in Forest's attacking play makes him an interesting option for managers looking beyond the most popular midfield picks.

His next few fixtures could make him even more appealing, especially if he continues to play an important role for Nottingham Forest. For now, he is certainly a player worth keeping an eye on.

Liverpool were another team expected to deliver in Gameweek 4, but they could only manage a goalless draw against Fulham.

The result was frustrating for managers who backed their attacking players, particularly with Liverpool playing at home. Their lack of goals also gives FPL managers a reason to look at their options more carefully.

That does not mean Liverpool players should be sold after one disappointing result. However, with other attacking options starting to emerge, their performances in the next few Gameweeks will be important.

Tottenham Hotspur's 0-0 draw with Everton was another frustrating result for FPL managers. Roberto De Zerbi's side have now failed to score in their opening four league matches, which is a major concern for their attacking players.

That makes Tottenham's forwards and midfielders difficult to trust at the moment. Their defence could still offer some value, but managers looking for goals and assists may have better options elsewhere.

Tottenham will need to find a way to improve in front of goal soon. Until that happens, FPL managers may be better off waiting before investing in their attacking players.

Leeds United's 4-1 win over Newcastle United was another result that caught the attention of FPL managers. Their attacking players produced a strong performance, while Newcastle United's defence struggled throughout the game.

The result gives Leeds some interesting options to watch, but managers should still be careful about chasing points after one big performance. Their players will need to show that they can produce regularly before becoming serious FPL targets.

After everything we saw in Gameweek 4, from Arsenal's continued strong form to Brighton's big win and the impressive performances from several individual players, which players have caught your attention?

Are you now considering bringing any of them into your FPL team for the next few Gameweeks? Share your thoughts in the comment section below.

title: Start 'Em, Sit 'Em running backs for Week 2 fantasy football
description: Running back is the most important spot in fantasy football. Here is the start/sit advice you need to give your team the best chance to win in Week 2.
fullText:
Every car needs a great engine.

You can have all the bells and whistles, from heated seats to a panoramic sunroof, but it all means nothing if the car is nothing more than the heaviest paperweight in the world. That's why some have gone back to basics, simply looking for something that gets them to and from a destination without issue.

In fantasy football, running backs are the engine.

You can't win without them. Strategies like "zero RB" in the draft are all the rage, but the games eventually prove that it's hard to win that way.

So you can have your fancy receivers, tight end and quarterback. Odds are, your championship aspirations rest on the running back spot – perhaps the greatest indication that fantasy doesn't always translate to reality.

As we flip the page to Week 2, here are the engines that you can trust at running back and others that should be left parked for the weekend.

Jordan Mason has been placed on injured reserve, paving the way for Jones to take full advantage. He is a capable runner and receiver, making him a dual-threat option for the Minnesota offense. With no clear backup to siphon away meaningful playing time, the 31-year-old should be plenty involved for Kevin O'Connell against the Bears.

And it's an inviting matchup for Jones' first game as the clear RB1. Chicago allowed the seventh-most fantasy points to running backs in Week 1, even in a game that mostly featured production through the air. Chuba Hubbard totaled two touchdowns in the opener for Carolina and Jones is seemingly game script proof in this one. For a game that is slated to feature plenty of offense, you'll definitely want the veteran in your lineup.

Montgomery delivered in a big way for fantasy managers last week, scoring three touchdowns in his Texans debut. There's no reason to believe that he can't produce at a high level again in Week 2. Despite fumbling issues for the Buccaneers in Week 1, Bucky Irving still delivered a great fantasy performance with 93 total yards and a touchdown despite Tampa trailing all afternoon.

The Texans will be eager for their defense to get on track against the Bengals, meaning we should anticipate a closer score. If he turns in another big game, Montgomery would be close to graduating into must-start territory. That is especially true for a player who even flashed some receiving upside in Week 1.

The Cowboys could've replaced their defenders with folding chairs in Week 1 and it would've had the same impact at a fraction of the cost. Nonexistent to the point where they couldn't even stop the same play multiple times on one drive, Dallas somehow looked worse than it did in 2025. That's hard to do, which brings us to Croskey-Merritt.

He had 63 rushing yards and a touchdown against a solid Philadelphia defensive line. More importantly, he had 16 carries. The man they call "Bill" will get even more running lanes in Dallas, especially after injuries piled up on defense against the Giants.

The Broncos shocked the football world in Kansas City – and not in a good way. Andy Reid essentially announced, with his play-calling, that he was going to run it with Kenneth Walker all night long and Denver still couldn't stop it. It turned out to be a debut to remember for Walker with 173 rushing yards and one touchdown. So shouldn't you trust Tuten in Week 2?

Well, not exactly. All of Jacksonville's production came from the right arm of Trevor Lawrence, despite a blowout victory for Liam Coen's team. Tuten did lead the backfield with 15 carries, but he was a non-factor in the passing game and couldn't get into the end zone. At the very least, Denver will try to avoid that type of embarrassment on the ground again. Steer clear of Tuten this week.

Lloyd stepped in as the replacement for Josh Jacobs, but his production came nowhere near what the veteran would've provided. The 25-year-old finished with 13 carries for just 37 yards. That is just 2.8 yards per carry, for those keeping score at home. With concerns along the offensive line, Lloyd has no clear path to produce at a high level.

Couple all of that with the threat of a running back by committee and it's even harder to trust Lloyd against a Jets defense that allowed just 47 rushing yards in Week 1 – even if it was only against the Titans.

Speaking of the Titans, yikes. We don't envy the position that team has put you in during the young season. Pollard was a nonfactor against the Jets, finishing with just 35 yards on the ground. Perhaps even more concerning, he couldn't even produce as a receiver in a trailing game script.

The Eagles defense represents a step up in class and there is absolutely no reason to believe the results will be any better. And since nothing ever happens when the Titans have the ball, we can't expect Pollard to magically produce out of nowhere.

title: Cam Ward presents another dangerous mobility test for Eagles' defense
description: Philadelphia must pressure Cam Ward without creating the same escape lanes Jayden Daniels exploited during the season opener
fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles spent part of Monday correcting the problems Jayden Daniels created outside the pocket. Their Week 2 opponent presents a similar concern.

Cam Ward combines high-level arm talent with enough mobility to punish undisciplined pass rushes.

Ward completed 19 of 32 passes for 140 yards and one touchdown during Tennessee's season-opening loss to the New York Jets. He also rushed four times for 21 yards, showing his ability to escape pressure and extend possessions. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio praised Ward's arm strength, athleticism, and continued development under Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll. Philadelphia understands the challenge after Daniels hurt the defense with his legs, particularly during Washington's final two possessions. Fangio specifically identified quarterback scrambling as one reason the Eagles struggled to close the game.

The Eagles recorded one sack and did not consistently win their individual pass-rush matchups. When pressure arrived, defenders occasionally created escape lanes by losing rush-lane integrity.

A good portion of the #Titans passing offense required Cam Ward to create outside of the pocket, between facing quick pressure, lack of open receivers, or bailing the pocket. #Eagles D-line will have to be discipline in their pass rush lanes to prevent big plays from happening… pic.twitter.com/wRLLPPjt0p

That cannot happen against Ward.

Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith Jr., Arnold Ebiketie, and Philadelphia's other edge defenders must pressure from controlled angles. Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, and Moro Ojomo must also compress the pocket without letting Ward escape through interior gaps. Tennessee allowed three sacks and scored only 10 points in Week 1, giving Philadelphia's rush a chance to improve. Pressure alone, however, will not be enough. The Eagles must finish plays. If Ward escapes the initial rush, he possesses the arm strength to find Calvin Ridley or Carnell Tate after coverage begins to break down.

Philadelphia's defensive plan must balance aggression with discipline.

title: Unbeaten no more: Moses Brown boys soccer falls to La Salle
description: Chase Deffley, Brad Laforest and Mickey Fernandez were all on target as La Salle posted a 3-1 triumph at Cimini Stadium on Wednesday.
fullText:
PROVIDENCE – Wednesday night brought a finishing touch La Salle has been missing at times early in this boys soccer season.

Strong stretches of play and quality chances have been common. This time the Rams were able to hit the back of the net with some regularity, knocking Moses Brown from the ranks of the unbeaten in Division I.

Chase Deffley, Brad Laforest and Mickey Fernandez were all on target as La Salle posted a 3-1 triumph at Cimini Stadium on Sept. 16. Each strike was more textbook than the last – Fernandez's volley in the 60th minute was the pick of the bunch on a mild evening.

"We've been looking for more goals," Fernandez said. "I've been trying to score more. I really attacked the ball, and I love finding the back of the net."

The Rams needed until the last two minutes to escape with a 1-0 win over East Providence last time out – they didn't leave it that late on this occasion. Deffley finished a lightning counterattack in the 23rd minute and Laforest doubled the advantage early in the second half. Fernandez made it 3-0 when he allowed an Avery Jefts pass off the right wing to drop over his hip before thumping a right-footed finish into the center of the cage.

"I practice volleys all the time," Fernandez said. "I haven't found that perfect sweet spot yet. I'm really glad it went in the back of the net."

It was Fernandez who set up Laforest for what turned out to be the winner. La Salle picked through the midfield with tic-tac-toe passing and Fernandez found Laforest darting free toward the left post. His simple finish into the open side of the net gave the Rams control of the night.

"He was through on net," Fernandez said. "I knew he had it. We've been looking for that all year."

Haven Knapp made a couple nice saves early for the Quakers before La Salle (3-0-1) broke through on the break. The move started in the left corner and went all the way down the pitch, with the Rams running at the retreating Moses Brown defense. Nate Jackson slipped Deffley through on the left for the opener to make it 1-0.

"We've been playing with each other for a while," Fernandez said. "It's good to have the group as a whole now playing as a team."

The Quakers (3-1-1) nearly had an equalizer in spectacular fashion late in the first half. Alex Holland took aim with a free kick from 35 yards and curled a right-footed shot that hit the crossbar above the top right corner. Anthony Gario pounced on a La Salle defensive mistake midway through the second half to put Moses Brown on the board.

MOSES BROWN (1): Anthony Gario.

LA SALLE (3): Chase Deffley, Brad LaForest, Mickey Fernandez; assists – Nate Jackson, Fernandez, Avery Jefts.

Halftime – LS, 1-0. Saves – Haven Knapp, MB, 7; Joseph Terlato, LS, 4.

title: Is football declining in popularity? New poll reveals competition
description: Gallup finds football still No. 1, soccer at a record high and a sharp football dip partly explained by when the poll was taken.
fullText:
Football still reigns supreme as the most popular sport in the U.S., but its grip might be loosening.

Gallup recently released results of its long-running poll tracking Americans' favorite sports to watch, and football came out well ahead of every other sport.

The poll, which was taken over Aug. 3-24, found that 31% of Americans say football is their favorite sport, 20 percentage points higher than any other sport.

The next tier, however, is much tighter.

Out of those surveyed, 11% picked basketball as their favorite sport, while 10% went with baseball and 9% chose soccer.

It's an all-time high for soccer's popularity in the U.S., which previously had never registered higher than 7%. As recently as 2007 the sport picked up just 2% of responses. Now soccer is nearly tied with two pillars of North American professional sports.

It still pales in comparison to football, though, which may be in a more precarious position than its lead suggests.

The 31% figure is, in fact, the lowest share of responses for football since 2001, when 28% picked the sport as their favorite. That year, basketball surged to a 16% share, its second highest ever, and 6% picked auto racing, an all-time high for the sport.

This year, football's share is also 10 points below the last Gallup poll in 2023, when 41% favored the sport.

It's also notable that this year's share is football's fourth lowest in the 24 polls since the sport took over the most popular sports crown from baseball in 1972.

Football's popularity, however, requires context.

The latest edition of the poll was run in August, prior to the start of football season. Based on Gallup's own numbers, football performs worse in the poll when it takes place outside of football season.

Since 1972, football has averaged a 38% share during the season. Meanwhile, that share dips to 32% outside of the sport's fall season. That suggests the timing of the poll may explain part of football's 10-point drop.

Still, this year's 31% number is lower than the out-of-season average.

Additionally, the poll is simply asking respondents for their favorite sport to watch. That means even if fewer Americans now rank football first, they may still be tuning into games.

Indeed, 16 of the top 25 spots in Nielsen's live sports telecast rankings for Aug. 31 through Sept. 6 were for Week 1 college football games — and the top telecast was the Wisconsin-Notre Dame tilt at Lambeau Field, which drew 7.4 million viewers.

And so, football still seems quite safe as America's favorite sport to watch for now — even if the latest poll shows a crack in its once-impregnable lead.

Methodology: USA TODAY created the above graphics using data from Gallup's recent favorite sport poll, where respondents were asked "What is your favorite sport to watch?"

title: Start 'Em, Sit 'Em D/STs for Week 2 fantasy football
description: Your D/ST selection in fantasy football can be the difference between winning and losing. Here are our start/sit recommendations for NFL Week 2.
fullText:
It's a word that has seen public opinion shift in recent years, going from a cheap new concept to something that is extracting every last dollar out of your wallet – especially if sports are your thing. Streaming was supposed to take away the need for cable, letting people buy what they want without breaking the bank.

And where did that get us? Right back to cable, but in streaming form.

Just like your viewing habits, picking the right fantasy football D/ST week to week is a lot like finding the right streamer. After all, few will find a unit that is startable every week of the season. If you do, be sure to hold on to it.

For the rest of us, we are left to play the matchups and hope for the best. At least in this case, the price isn't going up every couple of months.

Here are the fantasy defenses to start and others that should sit in Week 2.

Cam Ward didn't turn the ball over in Week 1, which could be problematic from a fantasy football standpoint. However, he could feel the need to force it in Week 2 as the Titans try to put together something that resembles an NFL offense.

One way or another, the Jets defense was living in the Tennessee backfield throughout Week 1 and Ward was running for his life. The second-year quarterback was slippery in the pocket, but the Eagles will present an even bigger challenge. This could be a big number from Vic Fangio's unit.

The Chiefs smothered the Broncos offense last week. Denver couldn't run the ball, couldn't throw the ball and, essentially, couldn't have the ball. It was an old-fashioned beatdown in Kansas City, reminding NFL fans of who the Chiefs are.

You could point to the new play-caller in Davis Webb for Denver, but this is still a much more talented unit than the one going into Arrowhead in Week 2. Daniel Jones seems to have lost some of the magic and Jonathan Taylor can't do it all alone. Steve Spagnuolo should be salivating at this matchup.

Flip the script. That is the goal for the Patriots in Week 2 after laying an egg against the Seahawks on opening night. New England had no business losing that game after Drew Lock entered for the injured Sam Darnold, but Mike Vrabel's team found a way anyway. It wasn't the defense's fault, however.

Despite some horrendous offense, the Patriots still held the Seahawks to just 13 points and we should expect more of the same against the Steelers. Aaron Rodgers isn't a threat to run and DK Metcalf will have to deal with Christian Gonzalez – and we know how that typically goes. With Rodgers averaging just 5.5 yards per attempt in Week 1, New England can crowd the line of scrimmage without much fear of being beat over the top.

The Bucs just gave up 33 points to the Bengals in Week 1, mostly because their offense produced more turnovers than your favorite bakery. It just so happens that Baker Mayfield was a key reason for that, losing three fumbles in the contest all by himself. One of Tampa's four turnovers did result in a touchdown, so we can't blame the defense for that.

Luckily for the Bucs, Week 2 is much easier against a lifeless Browns team. If a Deshaun Watson-led offense puts together a solid showing and ruins the day for this fantasy defense, we'll just have to tip our cap. Don't bet on that happening though.

It was a week to forget for one of the NFL's best defenses. Houston gave up 36 points and recorded just two sacks against Buffalo in Week 1, and they failed to force a turnover. You can easily dismiss the performance since the Bills were on the opposite sideline, but the Texans' Week 2 opponent is no cupcake.

The Bengals scored 33 points in the opener and that was without Ja'Marr Chase making an impact. While there's a good chance that the Texans were the first defense off the board in your draft, we can't in good faith recommend starting them. If there's a better matchup available, don't hesitate to take it.

Life without Micah Parsons hasn't been kind to the Packers. They are now on a five-game losing streak without the star defender, which is actually six if you include the game when he got hurt. Green Bay is in danger of stretching that streak to seven in the Meadowlands, where it will take on a frisky Jets team that is riding high after Week 1.

With some rain in the forecast, that bodes well for the Jets. They can lean on a solid offensive line and another run-heavy game script against a Packers team that just gave up a pair of rushing scores in the opener. And who could possibly forget the 22 unanswered points that the Vikings scored in the fourth quarter? Don't be surprised if that hangs over Matt LaFleur's group in Week 2.

Speaking of teams that deserve a little more credit, how about the Cardinals? No one gave them a chance to win in Week 1. Not only did they win, but they also did it in dominant fashion against the Super Bowl-contending Chargers. Now for an encore, Arizona only has to match up against the defending Super Bowl champions.

However, let's not forget that Lock is the starter and that increases the potential for turnovers from the Seahawks offense. Turnovers lead to short fields, short fields lead to points, points lead to fantasy defense sadness. Yet that isn't the Cardinals' only chance in Week 2, considering Mike LaFleur has put together a competent offense. This could be a letdown spot for the Seahawks after celebrating the Super Bowl win and losing Darnold all in one night. This will be their first test without him for an entire game, against a divisional opponent. Seattle's defense can ride the bench this week.

Myles Garrett was invisible in Week 1. He will miss Week 2 after knee surgery. Garrett might not be the only star in this loaded L.A. defense, but he is certainly the biggest one. The Giants won't have to deal with the pass-rusher, which only helps their chances.

John Harbaugh's team proved to be a physical, pesky group in Week 1. Between Jaxson Dart's legs and Cam Skattebo's tough running style, these aren't the Giants of old. After playing in Australia last week, the Giants are one of those teams that Sean McVay's sleepy bunch won't want to see. This game could be closer than expected and that won't bode well for the Rams' D/ST unit.

title: Why EFL matches get postponed for international call-ups
description: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why some League One and League two matches get postponed due to international call-ups.
fullText:
Matches in League One and League Two can be postponed during international breaks due to players being selected for international matches.

The English Football League (EFL) allows clubs to postpone fixtures should they receive a sufficient number of call-ups.

At least three of players have to be selected for their country's senior, under-21, under-20 or under-19 sides in order to request a postponement.

Players who are named on international standby lists or long lists will not count towards the three players at the time of announcement.

International age group players only qualify if they have been named in the starting XI, or been a named substitute making an appearance prior to the 75th minute, in either:

50% of a club's first-team matches

four of the last five first-team matches

If a player is signed by a club in either late August or during the January transfer window and they then get called up, a pro rata basis is used to determine if that player is available.

A team is also allowed to request a postponement if both the first and second choice goalkeepers are called up too.

Players signed on loan also count.

As per Fifa's guidelines, players selected must be released by their clubs by the Monday morning ahead of the first international fixtures of that window.

For home clubs wishing to request a postponement, they must do so at least five days prior to the game they wish to postpone.

Away teams must submit a request seven days in advance.

title: Klopp wants German team to help reclaim national pride from far-right
description: Jurgen Klopp said on Thursday that Germany's football team can help ensure "national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people" after a recent far-right AfD election victory. While not mentioning the AfD by name, Klopp advocated for adopting "positive patriotism", while saying: "I don't want to entrust national pride to the wrong people.
fullText:
Jurgen Klopp said on Thursday that Germany's football team can help ensure "national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people" after a recent far-right AfD election victory.

In a Frankfurt press conference announcing his first squad as Germany manager, the former Liverpool coach referenced a recent state election landslide win by the anti-immigration Alternative for Germany party.

The AfD won almost 44 percent of the vote in the former East German state of Saxony-Anhalt on September 6 and expects strong results in elections Sunday in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

Klopp took over the Germany job in July after the four-time World Cup winners suffered a third straight early elimination at the tournament.

The 59-year-old has often spoke out about social issues during his time as manager of Liverpool, Borussia Dortmund and Mainz.

While not mentioning the AfD by name, Klopp advocated for adopting "positive patriotism", while saying: "I don't want to entrust national pride to the wrong people.

"A crazy amount of things have happened not that long ago. There was a vote which some people probably found OK, but others would have thought 'good heavens, what's going on here?'"

"From the perspective of someone in sport, I'd like to reclaim the flag for myself and for us. When we wave it, I don't want that someone thinks 'what's going on with you?'

"I want that they think you're happy and you understand how lucky you are to be born in this wonderful country or to have moved here and live here."

Topics involving patriotism and nationalism are often sensitive in Germany, a country still at pains to atone for its dark history of Nazi rule, World War II and the Holocaust.

Speaking of national pride, Klopp said he was "not even sure if one can -- or is allowed to -- use that term anymore without it being misunderstood".

"I can be proud of being German and still be open, diverse, kind and friendly."

The coach said it was more important that the country had enough doctors and caregivers, but said football can "foster a sense of community here, allowing us to truly feel the power of sport".

On Thursday, Klopp took the unusual step of naming a huge 44-man squad for four upcoming Nations League matches, despite matchday lists being restricted to 23 players.

"It's very unusual that you've got four games in two weeks with the national team," Klopp said.

"I want to get to know as many players as possible in that time."

Klopp won the Champions League and Premier League during a trophy-laden nine-year stint at Liverpool.

title: Kenny Minchey’s mindset excites Will Stein amid offensive struggles
description: Revaluating QB Kenny's poise, muddy pockets, and key growth moments against Alabama's elite pass rush.
fullText:
So, I took a look back at the offensive game film from Saturday, and there really isn't a lot to be happy about. Only three drives went over 20 yards, and the Cats' 3rd-down offense was some of the worst I've seen.

All 10 of Kentucky's offensive points came off Alabama turnovers. That is not going to get it done in the SEC.

It starts up front; the line was mostly bad, but the tackle spot was the worst. Heard and Wood were supposed to be anchors, and unfortunately for Kentucky, I think they took it literally Saturday. They were slow to fire off the ball, and Alabama's edge pressure blitzed them. That can't happen going forward, but Kenny Minchey didn't have his best game on Saturday either.

The biggest takeaway from the coaching staff this week isn't about Minchey's arm talent; it's about his mentality.

After throwing an early pick-six, Minchey could have folded up shop and allowed it to continue to bother him. Instead, Kenny kept competing and trying to get better. Will Stein praised his ability to isolate each down, playing with a "one-play focus" rather than letting past mistakes snowball into new ones.

The SEC is an unforgiving league, and the pocket isn't going to get any cleaner, especially if the line can't improve drastically. The coaching staff is hammering home the importance of operating in "muddy pockets" and knowing when to simply live to fight another down.

There was a specific sequence in the Alabama game that Will Stein called Minchey out on. He could have stepped up and thrown the ball away to avoid a loss of yardage. Instead, he held the ball and got sacked.

"That is where that's a growth opportunity for him," Stein noted. "The right play is to throw the ball away. It's not to try to do something outside of the realm of the offense."

Minchey was 18-for-31 for 146 yards, throwing one pick and one TD, averaging just eight yards per completion. That means nearly everything was either incomplete or dink-and-dunk. Good defenses aren't going to allow you to consistently drive the ball down the field meticulously. You have to hit the home run ball, and it's not going to get any easier for Minchey on Saturday.

Playing in front of 100,000 screaming fans in College Station will be another massive test for a rebuilt line and a new starting QB. But time on task is everything at the quarterback position. Seeing the speed of an elite defense this past weekend should slow the game down for the offense moving forward. Minchey took his lumps, but his mindset proves he's exactly the kind of guy BBN wants under center.

title: Real Madrid midfield duo leave last season’s controversy behind them
description: Peace has returned to the Real Madrid dressing room. One of the biggest conflicts within the squad, and arguably the most serious of all, now appears to be a thing of the past.Ineed, as reported by MA...
fullText:
Peace has returned to the Real Madrid dressing room. One of the biggest conflicts within the squad, and arguably the most serious of all, now appears to be a thing of the past.

Ineed, as reported by MARCA, Aurelien Tchouameni and Federico Valverde have put their differences behind them, providing a clear sign of that during the match against Elche.

The Frenchman and the Uruguayan were involved in one of the most serious arguments in the Real Madrid dressing room last season.

The incident took place in May during a training session. A disagreement on the pitch escalated and eventually continued inside the dressing room, with Valverde subsequently requiring hospital treatment after suffering a head injury in the confrontation.

Burying the hatchet. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

The episode highlighted the turmoil within a Real Madrid squad that was already struggling, with then-manager Alvaro Arbeloa attempting to calm a situation that had spiralled out of control.

The arrival of Jose Mourinho in the dugout appears to have brought a change in atmosphere, however, and the relationship between Tchouaméni and Valverde now seems to have been repaired.

Their behaviour after the victory over Elche, which was the first instance of the pair starting together since the incident in May, offered perhaps the clearest evidence yet.

At the final whistle, Tchouameni and Valverde were seen high-fiving each other before embracing, putting their previous differences firmly behind them.

The gesture came after an important victory for Real Madrid, who secured the points they needed to remain in touch with Barcelona at the top of the table.

Whatever happened between the two midfielders last season now appears to have been left in the past, with their post-match exchange providing a visible sign of a calmer atmosphere inside Mourinho's dressing room.

One of the biggest objective for Mourinho, who returned to the club for his second stint in the summer, was to unite the locker room, especially given the reports of disharmony and discontent during the last season.

While there is still work to be done, early signs indicate that the Portuguese tactician has managed to set some things right and install order, discipline, and unity in the dressing room.

title: ‘Loser’ – Cleveland Browns fans hit back over Deshaun Watson’s ‘disrespectful’ comments

title: A look at the Guardians' playoff race standing in AL Central, wild card
description: The Guardians have a final, nine-game push in their hopes of securing a playoff spot. Here, we set up the Central and wild card playoff races.
fullText:
CLEVELAND — They say every win or loss counts the same in a 162-game season, but there's also no denying that everything becomes hyper-concentrated in late September, when the remaining games dwindle and the exact playoff scenarios come into focus.

To that end, there's little doubt the Guardians just won the biggest series of their season — to date, at least.

Cleveland (78-75) rallied in back-to-back games to win a three-games series Sept. 14-16 against the White Sox (77-75) and, in doing so, overtook Chicago for the American League Central lead. It's the first time the Guardians have led the division since July 4.

"Oh, it's awesome," said Petey Halpin, who hit a go-ahead three-run home run in Cleveland's 6-3 win in the series finale to take the division lead. "Playoff push, fighting for the first place in the division and just the energy we have in the locker room, the clubhouse, just going out on the field, it's great."

It sets up a wild, week-and-a-half dash to the finish line. The winner of the Sept. 16 game at Progressive Field took the AL Central lead, while the loser slotted into the third and final wild card spot in the American League bracket.

Both the Guardians and White Sox are racing each other. They're also trying to hold off the Texas Rangers, Toronto Blue Jays and Baltimore Orioles for the No. 6 seed.

As of the conclusion of the Sept. 16 game, the Guardians had a 58.7% chance of winning the division and an 82.4% chance of making the playoffs, according to FanGraphs' projections. The White Sox were given a 41.4% chance to win the AL Central and a 73.5% chance to make the playoffs.

Here's where those races stand entering Sept. 17.

Nine games remain for the Guardians:

Ten games remain for the White Sox:

four against the Detroit Tigers

three against the Colorado Rockies to finish the season

The White Sox have the single easiest remaining schedule among any contender at .433 the rest of the way, plus they have an extra game to play against that easier slate, putting them in a prime position for a playoff spot. They're in the driver's seat, but they've been struggling as of late. They also led in both losses in Cleveland this week, leaving a lasting feeling of an opportunity wasted and momentum slipping away.

Considering the standings, the schedules and the lack of time remaining, both AL Central teams are in positive spots.

The Yankees (88-64) and Boston Red Sox (82-70) are cruising to the top two wild card spots, assuming they don't catch the Tampa Bay Rays (92-59) for the AL East title. Regardless, it looks clear the AL East will have at least three playoff teams, leaving one wild card spot up for grabs.

That final slot is likely to go to the loser of the Guardians-White Sox race in the Central, or the Blue Jays (76-77), Rangers (76-76) or Orioles (75-78).

Interestingly enough, the last three teams fighting for a wild card spot have several games against one another remaining on the schedule.

A number of tiebreakers could come into play for the Guardians. To note, Major League Baseball no longer utilizes play-in games after the extension of the playoff bracket to six teams in each league.

For the AL Central race, the White Sox hold the tiebreaker(head-to-head season record) over the Guardians. Because the White Sox hold the tiebreaker, have an extra game remaining and are only down 0.5 games, technically they still control their own destiny despite the Guardians leading the race.

Also of note, the Houston Astros, who are leading the AL West, also own the tiebreaker over the Guardians. This would come into play if both teams win their divisions and are vying for the No. 2 seed, which would come with a first-round bye in the playoffs. The No. 3 seed (the division winner with the worst record) would play the No. 6 seed in the first round, known as the Wild Card Series.

In the wild card race, the Blue Jays and Rangers both hold the tiebreaker over the Guardians, but Cleveland holds the tiebreaker over the Orioles.

title: Lampard on Amenda, momentum and Forest
description: Coventry boss Frank Lampard has been speaking to the media before Saturday's Premier League game against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground (kick-off 17:30 BST).  Swiss defender Aurele Amenda is likely to be unavailable for Saturday's game after picking up a calf injury during the Carabao Cup loss to Aston Villa.  "He will be scanned over the next 24 hours or so," said Lampard, who added that it is a blow as Amenda is a good player who makes an impact on and off the pitch.
fullText:
Coventry boss Frank Lampard has been speaking to the media before Saturday's Premier League game against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground (kick-off 17:30 BST).

Here are the key lines from his news conference:

Swiss defender Aurele Amenda is likely to be unavailable for Saturday's game after picking up a calf injury during the Carabao Cup loss to Aston Villa. "He will be scanned over the next 24 hours or so," said Lampard, who added that it is a blow as Amenda is a good player who makes an impact on and off the pitch.

It is important to Lampard that Coventry are adaptable with formation: "You have a look at the opposition and you see what you feel is the best opportunity to try to get the best out of our team."

Lampard reflected on his side's 3-1 defeat by Villa: "The critical part of the game was set pieces which we gave away. I thought we competed well in phases of the game and specifically the first half and the reaction to going 1-0 down. [We] scored a great, great goal, pushed and created a really good atmosphere in the stadium. Critical things we have to get right."

On club captain Matt Grimes: "He is a great professional, great around team-mates, calm head, very good player. Played a lot of years in the Championship, was very experienced at it and can play for me at any level and now he is integral to everything we do here as a person and as a player."

Lampard said the extended international break is positive in some part as it will allow players who are injured or arrived late in the window to get fit with more training time. But, it means he does not have a complete squad: "It's just one we will manage physically but I think the opportunity to get players fit is a good thing for us."

When asked about keeping up the positive momentum from last season's promotion, he said: "We just have to because it is football. We have been privileged for a while to win a lot of football matches here. It is more difficult when you don't [win], that makes the job of all of ours tougher because that is what we are here for and what you want to do and sometimes it is human nature to feel down but we just have to focus on the work that we have got to do to keep trying to improve, to keep trying to get results."

On Nottingham Forest: "They've got a high-quality squad, we have to be careful. Always good in transition, always good to play vertical and play forward and really talented people between lines, it's a really good system with players that [Oliver Glasner] has got there that suit the system that he is playing, hence it will be a tough match."

title: Jaguars embrace ‘our reality’ of playing on the road for 28 of their next 33 games
description: “This is our truth; this is our reality. And nobody in this league and in this fanbase is going to care at the end of the day." - Jaguars coach Liam Coen
fullText:
That was Jacksonville Jaguars coach Liam Coen's message to his team months ago. He wanted to establish a tone for what could be the most daunting stretch in NFL history.

The Jaguars (1-0) will play 28 of their next 33 regular-season games away from home, beginning Sunday at Denver (0-1).

"Drop us off in a plane and we'll go play," Coen said.

Because of an ongoing, $1.4 billion renovation to EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, the Jaguars will play two of their eight home games this season in London. They will play the entire 2027 schedule outside the city, with nine homes games spread between Orlando, London and potentially another international site.

>>> STREAM ACTION SPORTS JAX 24/7 LIVE <<<

It's far from ideal, but hardly a concern for a team that believes it has the talent to compete in any venue and against any opponent. And Coen chose to embrace it.

"If you're a part of this organization right now, this is the reality," Coen said. "This is our truth; this is our reality. And nobody in this league and in this fanbase is going to care at the end of the day. Like, nobody.

"It's not going to be an allowed excuse or an allowed reason because the results are what they are at the end of the season. Your record's your record, and nobody's going to look at it and say, 'Oh, well, they had to go play a lot of games away from home.'"

Coen addressed the team's future with players and coaches before training camp. Now, it's become a version of "trauma bonding," center Robert Hainsey said.

"He definitely made it our mentality," Hainsey said. "Like, literally, drop us off anywhere, put the ball down and let's play. That's how we got to prepare. That's who we got to be. This is the NFL. It's never easy. It's just one more thing that's going to make it maybe a little bit tougher."

The Jaguars return home on Sept. 27 against New England, and then they are away for an entire month — at Cincinnati, two home games in the United Kingdom, followed by a bye week. After another home game on Nov. 1, they have three straight road games.

The Jags requested "a little bit of a donut in the middle of the schedule" to allow construction teams to get work done inside the stadium, team president Mark Lamping said.

Jacksonville also closes the season with four of its final six on the road.

[DOWNLOAD: Free Action News Jax app for alerts as news breaks]

"In your head, you're kind of feeling sorry for yourself, 'This sucks, blah, blah, blah.' But I know everyone next to me is doing it, too," Hainsey said. "Yeah, we're going to complain about it, but it's a little bit of an outlet and we have fun with it. And then, when we bring it back, it's like, 'Let's go play.'"

The Jaguars played well on the road in 2025, finishing 6-2. Their biggest win: at Denver a few days before Christmas.

"Like coach says, 'Anytime, anyplace,'" cornerback Jourdan Lewis said. "We want to play to our standard regardless of where it is."

Coen, whose team is coming off an AFC South title, is always looking for motivation to keep his guys playing with an edge. The team's less-than-ideal stadium situation could help.

"When you go on the road, especially the West Coast trips that we did have last year, those are longer trips," Coen said. "You're together a little bit longer. … You can get a little bit more rest and less distractions.

"As much as I want to go see my family on a Saturday after we have our work done here, it is good for us. It's good for us to be connected. It's good for us to be around each other and to keep learning and growing together."

title: Wolves and Albion issue warning over derby disorder
description: The clubs issue a statement ahead of Sunday's meeting after trouble flared when the teams last met.
fullText:
Wolves and West Bromwich Albion have stressed ahead of their first league meeting in five years that there will be serious consequences for supporters who engage in violence and disorder.

In a joint statement issued before Sunday's Championship match at Molineux, they said trouble at an FA Cup meeting between the clubs in 2024 saw 43 people arrested, 12 charged and sentenced and five given permanent club bans.

Play at The Hawthorns two years ago was halted for 38 minutes after police were assaulted, missiles were thrown and flares were set off.

Wolves and Albion said supporters could "expect enhanced stewarding, policing, robust ticketing controls and additional safety measures" on Sunday.

The clubs stated on Thursday that outcomes following 2024's cup match demonstrated "disorder, violence and criminal behaviour carry significant consequences and will continue to be dealt with robustly" by them and police.

Wolves won the tie two years ago in what was the first match between the clubs in front of fans since 2012.

The clubs said they had worked "closely with the Safety Advisory Group, local authorities and police to ensure appropriate arrangements" were in place for Sunday's Championship game, which kicks off at 12:00 BST.

Fans were "reminded that anyone found engaging in violence, discriminatory behaviour, entering the pitch or trackside areas, throwing missiles, using pyrotechnics or breaching ground regulations risks arrest, prosecution, football banning orders and long-term or permanent exclusion from their club".

The two clubs asked supporters to only use tickets bought through official channels and to sit in the correct designated home or away area.

"Anyone found attempting to access, or being in an incorrect area, will be refused entry or ejected and may face further sanction," they added.

The clubs also asked fans to arrive in good time to allow for security searches and stadium entry procedures, follow instructions of stewards and police and report any unsafe, discriminatory or anti-social behaviour.

They said: "The overwhelming majority of Albion and Wolverhampton Wanderers supporters attend this fixture to support their team passionately and responsibly, and we are confident that will once again be the case."

title: ‘Not a robot, but used to tough calls’: Samson on Sooryavanshi competition, relentless scrutiny and the fight for his place in XI
description: Sanju Samson addressed the difficulty of achieving consistency in the T20 format. He explained that a fearless mindset is crucial for maintaining focus and performance. Samson acknowledged that team management faces tough decisions regarding player selection. He stated that he understands these choices from his IPL captaincy experience. Samson also mentioned that he is experienced enough to handle external commentary.
fullText:
NEW DELHI: The 'inconsistent' tag has long followed Sanju Samson. He made his T20I debut as a 20-year-old in 2015 but his place in the Indian team is never assured. On Tuesday night, after scoring his first half-century since the dream run in the T20 World Cup in March, Samson highlighted the difficulty of achieving consistency with a high-risk approach necessary in T20Is.

"You can't control the consistency in the result in this format. Consistency has to be in the frame of mind. I think that's what 'fearless mindset' is called," Samson said after scoring a 57 off 22 that helped India seal the series against Afghanistan here. The last T20I of the series will be played on Thursday.

With India's T20I team boasting of three other equally destructive openers — Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi — Samson's place in the team is always under scrutiny. Two months ago, he was benched in England when Sooryavanshi played ahead of him. Samson, who will be 32 years old in another two months, said the experience of taking hard calls as an IPL captain helped him understand the team management's position on Sooryavanshi.

"It's not easy to run an Indian team. A 15-year-old boy has scored 700-800 runs in the IPL. My World Cup was before that. He had to come in some or the other manner," he said. "I didn't perform in 2-3 games and he was in form and we wanted to win games in that series. I have been in this situation and I have taken tough calls as a captain in the IPL."

Samson, however, did concede that he gets affected at times. "At first, it feels bad. I am not a machine. I am not a robot. It definitely matters. And you kind of get a bit affected. But then you try to talk to yourself and tell that what you are and what you need to do," he said.

"I try to turn off the Wi-Fi. But sometimes the Wi-Fi turns on and I see the comments of the senior players," Samson said of the endless debate over his spot in the XI. "It's their choice. They can use a positive frame of sentences or they can use a negative frame of sentences. I think I am experienced enough to handle it."

title: Baur given first Germany call as Klopp scours for new talent
description: Celtic midfielder Mika Baur has given a first senior Germany call-up as new head coach Jurgen Klopp unveiled an unprecedented 44-man squad for upcoming Nations League matches.  The 22-year-old, who has already played for his country at youth level up to under-21s and joined the Scottish champions from Paderborn this summer, is one of 16 players to be handed their first call-ups by the former Liverpool manager.  Teams are restricted to naming 20 outfield players and three goalkeepers for each match, but Klopp has split the group into two separate squads for their four upcoming fixtures.
fullText:
Celtic midfielder Mika Baur has given a first senior Germany call-up as new head coach Jurgen Klopp unveiled an unprecedented 44-man squad for upcoming Nations League matches.

The 22-year-old, who has already played for his country at youth level up to under-21s and joined the Scottish champions from Paderborn this summer, is one of 16 players to be handed their first call-ups by the former Liverpool manager.

Teams are restricted to naming 20 outfield players and three goalkeepers for each match, but Klopp has split the group into two separate squads for their four upcoming fixtures.

The first group will be available for the games fixtures against the Netherlands in Amsterdam on 24 September and at home to Greece three days later in Augsburg.

The second group, which includes Baur, will be available for Germany's matches against Serbia in Munich on 1 October and Greece in Thessaloniki on 4 October.

"It's very unusual that you've got four games in two weeks with the national team," Klopp said.

"I want to get to know as many players as possible in that time. It's not an A-team and a B-team, but the two squads have been created in a way that each fits well together."

Klopp replaced Julian Nagelsmann in July after the four-time World Cup winners were eliminated at the last-32 stage of the World Cup, their third successive early exit from the tournament.

"It really felt like you had the feeling after the World Cup that German football is on its knees and we have no talents, no footballers," Klopp said.

"In the past four weeks, as we've been looking closely, plenty of talents have caught our eye.

"It's a squad for two or three years from now, not just for the next four international games."

title: Cardiff boosted by return of Wales defender Lawlor
description: Wales defender Dylan Lawlor returns from injury to boost winless Cardiff City against Charlton Athletic in the Championship.
fullText:
Cardiff City's bid for a first Championship win of the season against Charlton Athletic has been boosted by the return of Wales defender Dylan Lawlor.

The 20-year-old has not yet featured in 2026-27 because of a knee injury but is back for the Bluebirds' home fixture against the Addicks on Saturday (12:30 BST).

Lawlor returned to training this week along with fellow centre-back Will Fish, who will not be risked after hernia surgery.

"Dylan will definitely be available, he's good to go," said Cardiff head coach Brian Barry-Murphy.

"Will Fish won't be available, he's probably another week behind so we're not going to take any chances, but Dylan's back fully fit."

How worried should Cardiff be about wasteful finishing?

Injury-hit Cardiff weighing up free-agent options

Lawlor made 43 appearances for club and country in 2025-26 but was left out of Wales' Nations League squad on Tuesday because of his injury.

The centre-back enjoyed a rapid rise to establish himself in the Bluebirds' side under Barry-Murphy in League One and the boss is weighing up his role against Charlton.

"He's trained really well. We'll see how he is today and tomorrow, then make a decision based on who we feel is best to start this game," said Barry-Murphy, whose side have drawn four and lost three of their seven league fixtures.

"But he's fully fit, with no issues with his knee whatsoever, and he looks great."

Lawlor's reappearance and Fish's impending return is good news for Cardiff, who have had to reshuffle their back line in order to deal with injuries.

In addition to the signing of Krystian Bielik from West Bromwich Albion, the Bluebirds have played full-backs Perry Ng and Joel Bagan in central positions in recent weeks.

With Gabriel Osho missing some games with his own injury, Barry-Murphy says Lawlor and Fish being back gives him much-needed selection choice.

"They're two such outstanding players and to give us that extra depth to our squad that we've lacked in the earliest parts of the season is going to be really important," he added.

"I'm very pleased to get them back and will try to build them up gradually to make sure that they stay fit, and both players can be very important for us."

Cardiff are still without injured Wales internationals Rubin Colwill and Isaak Davies as well as defender Calum Chambers.

Chambers has knee, neck and back issues but Colwill and Davies are close to returns from their respective ankle and hamstring problems.

"We expect them to train in the middle of the international break, Rubin and Isaak," said Barry-Murphy.

"Calum Chambers is having a further scan on his injury this afternoon, so we'll know more on the timescale."

title: Garnacho overlooked again as Emery admits others ahead of him
description: Alejandro Garnacho is down Aston Villa's pecking order as he battles to make an impression.  The winger was an unused substitute in Wednesday's 3-1 Carabao Cup win at Coventry, the third successive game he has been left on the bench.  The 22-year-old has played just 31 minutes in three substitute appearances since his loan move from Chelsea and is being kept out by George Hemmings.
fullText:
Alejandro Garnacho is down Aston Villa's pecking order as he battles to make an impression.

The winger was an unused substitute in Wednesday's 3-1 Carabao Cup win at Coventry, the third successive game he has been left on the bench.

The 22-year-old has played just 31 minutes in three substitute appearances since his loan move from Chelsea and is being kept out by George Hemmings.

Villa hold a conditional obligation to buy Garnacho for about £42.5m, believed to be tied to appearances, and boss Unai Emery wants to see improvement.

"Continue working. Work, work, train, work," he said.

"When he can have minutes to play, try to play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now.

"George is playing fantastic. Alysson is also understanding things well and is giving us things I want. (Ibrahim) Mbaye also responded well.

"We want a competitive team and players to compete in the style we have. Garnacho is a little bit behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs."

Garnacho's pre-season, after arriving at Villa Park in July, was disrupted by a facial injury he suffered against BG Pathum United. It meant he missed the Super Cup defeat by Paris St-Germain in August.

Emery has made 14 substitutions in Villa's past three games, with Garnacho overlooked, and he was not one of the seven changes for the win at the CBS Arena.

Two goals from Tammy Abraham and Ross Barkley's header earned Villa a fourth-round trip to Bournemouth in October.

title: Six-time Grand Slam champion Salisbury retires
description: Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury retires from professional tennis.
fullText:
Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury has retired from professional tennis.

Salisbury chose this month's US Open as his final event and reached the semi-finals with his long-time partner Rajeev Ram, who had also decided to retire.

The venue was fitting, as in 2023 Salisbury and Ram became the first pair in history to win three consecutive US Open men's doubles titles.

Salisbury is Britain's most successful men's doubles player of the Open Era. He also won the 2020 Australian Open with Ram, and two mixed doubles titles with Desirae Krawczyk.

The 34-year-old says he has been thinking about his future for a while, and is now "very happy with the decision."

"Tennis has been my life for as long as I can remember and I have been incredibly fortunate to have had all the opportunities, experiences and success that I have," he posted on Instagram.

"To be able to travel the world and call playing tennis my job has been a dream come true and I never believed I could have lived the life and had the career that I have.

"I gave it my all and know I can be proud and look back with no regrets."

Salisbury took a three month break at the start of this year, having told BBC Sport about the anxiety which had been affecting him on tour.

While he did not think it affected his tennis very much, he said it left him with a "feeling of dread" which made life on the road far less enjoyable.

Salisbury finishes his career with 17 tour level titles, including the season ending ATP Finals of 2022 and 2023.
